summary: Montgomery Schuyler was an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson, earning degrees up to 1900. He served as a Fellow at Columbia University from 1900 to 1902.
Moodeen Sheriff worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moreton John Walhouse was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at East India Company College (1841–1842) and served in the Indian Civil Service (~1840–1873), including as Judge of Mangalore in the Madras Presidency until 1873.

Moriichi Yamazaki works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman. His posts include Professor at Sendai National College of Technology and roles at Hosen Gakuen College and Chuo Academic Research Institute.

Moritz Abraham Stern was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller, later serving at Göttingen as Extraordinarius from 1829 to 1884.

Moritz Spitzer was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna and Kiel University, earning his Ph.D. under Friedrich Otto Schrader in 1926. He worked as an Assistant at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1927 to 1928.

Moritz Steinschneider worked in linguistics and other fields, studying under Franz Bopp, Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, and at the University of Leipzig (PhD ~1850). His posts included director at Jüdische Mädchenschule Berlin (1869–1890) and assistant at the Royal Danish Library (1869).

Moriz Haupt specialized in linguistics and other fields, studying under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at Leipzig (1837–1851) and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1853), and served as perpetual secretary of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Friedrich Max Müller. He held posts at the University of Oxford, Charles University/German University in Prague, and Visva-Bharati University.

Linguist Morris Swadesh studied at the University of Chicago under Leonard Bloomfield and Yale University under Edward Sapir. He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, City College of New York, National Autonomous University of Mexico, and University of Alberta.

Morten Schlütter works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen, Komazawa University, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein, and has held teaching posts at Yale, Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, Wisconsin-Madison, and University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at University College London, he served as Director of the National Museum Cardiff and Museum of London, Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1944–1948), and professor at the University of London.

Morton Klass worked in religious studies, Indology, and other fields. He studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, and under Conrad M. Arensberg. He held faculty positions at Bennington College, Columbia University, and Barnard College (~1969–1997).

Morton W. Easton was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Columbia and Yale, completing his Ph.D. under William Dwight Whitney in 1872, and held professorships at the University of Tennessee (1871–1881) and the University of Pennsylvania (1882–1912).
Mother Sayamagyi was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who was a disciple of and succeeded Sayagyi U Ba Khin.

Motohiro Yoritomi was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He held academic posts at Shuchiin University (1973–2011), Kyoto University, Ryukoku University, and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Motoi Ono is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tsukuba under Yasunori Ejima and earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, later becoming an associate professor at Tsukuba in 1995.
Moumita Hossain works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Ranjit Sen and is attested in 2026 as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Mountstuart Elphinstone was a historian and Indologist educated at the Royal High School. He served with the East India Company from ~1795 to 1796, at the Court of the Peshwa, and as Governor at the University of Mumbai (1819–1827).

Mrinal Kaul is an Indologist and philosopher educated at St. Stephen's College, Pune, Delhi, Oxford, and Concordia University. His posts include lecturer at Naples "L'Orientale", assistant professor at Manipal Academy, and associate professor at IIT Bombay.
